Maladaptive Strategies.value: I spend long hours on my phone, games, or internet to avoid thinking
I pick arguments or create drama to distract myself from the trauma
Making any plans for the future

Threat.value: I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
I feel unsafe unless my back is against a wall where I can see the room
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

Memory.value: Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger
There are parts of the event that I simply cannot remember no matter how hard I try
My memories of the frightening event are like a film that plays over and over.

Negative Appraisals.value: I can't trust that I will do the right thing

issues.item: Threat: Irritability: Irritable behavior, angry outbursts, or acting aggressively
issues.explanation: 'Irritability' is not a threat appraisal/perception item; it reflects arousal/behavioral dysregulation and fits better outside the Threat node. In this profile, the other Threat items are coherent terrorism-related hypervigilance/safety behaviors ('Scanning Exits', 'Back to Wall'), so this item is internally mismatched within the node and weakly aligned with the formulation in which Memory-linked threat should reflect perceived current danger rather than aggressive behavior.

vignette: Kofi had always taken pride in his work as a tailor, carefully crafting each garment with precision and attention to detail. But that was before the terrorist attack at the market where he used to buy fabric. The sounds of gunfire and screams still echoed in his mind, and the smell of smoke and blood lingered on his clothes. In the aftermath, Kofi found himself struggling to make sense of what had happened. He couldn't shake off the feeling that he was weak for not being able to protect himself or others (Weakness Belief). This self-doubt crept into every aspect of his life, making him question his ability to trust his own judgment (Self-Doubt). As a result, Kofi began to feel like he no longer belonged anywhere (Belong Nowhere), as if the attack had somehow severed his connection to the world around him. These negative appraisals took a toll on Kofi's daily life. He started spending long hours on his phone, scrolling through social media or playing games, in an attempt to distract himself from the memories of that day (Screen Escape). He would also pick arguments with his friends and family, creating drama as a way to shift his focus away from the trauma (Seeking Conflict). Making plans for the future seemed daunting, so Kofi simply avoided thinking about it altogether (Avoid Future Plans). But despite these attempts to escape, the memories of the attack lingered. Sometimes Kofi would recall the event in vivid detail, only to feel a strange sense of numbness, as if he was watching someone else's life unfold (Emotionless Recall). Other times, he would find himself stuck on specific moments, reliving them over and over like a film playing on repeat (Memory Replay). There were also gaps in his memory, moments that seemed lost forever, which only added to his frustration (Memory Gaps). These memories not only haunted Kofi but also made him hypervigilant. He would scan for exits whenever he entered a room or building (Scanning Exits), and feel safest when his back was against a wall, where he could see everything around him (Back to Wall). His constant state of alertness left him exhausted, yet he couldn't shake off the feeling that danger lurked around every corner (Hypervigilance). As Kofi's memories continued to plague him, they also reinforced his negative appraisals. He began to believe that he was indeed weak for not being able to overcome these memories (Weakness Belief). His self-doubt grew, and with it, the conviction that he no longer belonged anywhere (Belong Nowhere). The threat of danger seemed omnipresent, and Kofi's maladaptive strategies only intensified. He became more withdrawn, avoiding social interactions and spending most of his time alone in his small apartment above the tailor shop. His work suffered as a result, with orders piling up and customers beginning to lose patience. It was this downward spiral that finally brought Kofi to seek help. He realized that he couldn't keep living in a state of constant fear and self-doubt. With a sense of trepidation, he began to hope that therapy might offer him a way out of the darkness that had consumed his life since the attack.
